stem: When gold crystallizes, it forms face-centred cubic cells. The unit cell edge length is 408 pm. Calculate the density of gold. Molar mass of gold is 197 g/mol.
solution:
\(\rho = \dfrac{M n}{a^3 N_A}\)

\(M = 197\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\), \(n = 4\) atoms for fcc, \(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\) atoms \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\),

\(a = 408\ \mathrm{pm} = 408 \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m} = 4.08 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}\)

Substitution of these quantities in the equation gives

\(\rho = \dfrac{197\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}} \times 4\ \text{atom}}{(4.08 \times 10^{-8})^3\ \mathrm{cm^3} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\ \text{atom}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}}\)

\(= 19.27\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}\), \(19.27 \times 10^{3}\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\).

stem: A compound made of elements C and D crystallizes in fcc structure. Atoms of C are present at the corners of the cube. Atoms of D are at the centres of faces of the cube. What is the formula of the compound?
solution:
i. C atoms are present at the 8 corners. The contribution of each corner atom to the unit cell is 1/8 atom. Hence, the number of C atom that belongs to the unit cell \(= 8 \times (1/8) = 1\)

ii. D atoms are present at the centres of six faces of unit cell. Each face-centre atom is shared between two cubes. Hence, contribution of each face centre atom to the unit cell is 1/2 atom.

The number of D atoms that belong to unit cell \(= 1/2 \times 6 = 3\)

There are one C atom and three D atoms in the unit cell.

\(\therefore\) Formula of compound \(= \mathrm{CD_3}\)

stem: The unit cell of metallic silver is fcc. If radius of Ag atom is 144.4 pm, calculate (a) edge length of unit cell (b) volume of Ag atom, (c) the percent of the volume of a unit cell, that is occupied by Ag atoms, (d) the percent of empty space.
solution:
(a) For fcc unit cell, \(r = 0.3535\,a\)

\(r = 144.4\ \mathrm{pm} = 144.4 \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m} = 144.4 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{cm}\)

\(a = \dfrac{r}{0.3535} = \dfrac{144.4 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{cm}}{0.3535} = 4.085 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}\)

(b) Volume of Ag atom \(= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \times 3.142 \times (144.4 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{cm})^3 = 1.261 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\)

(c) In fcc unit cell, there are 4 Ag atoms.

Volume occupied by 4 Ag atoms \(= 4 \times 1.26 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 5.044 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\)

Total volume of unit cell \(= a^3 = (4.085 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm})^3 = 6.817 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\)

Percent of volume occupied by Ag atoms \(= \dfrac{\text{volume occupied by atoms in unit cell}}{\text{total volume of unit cell}} \times 100 = \dfrac{5.044 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}}{6.817 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}} \times 100 = 74\%\)

(d) Percent empty space \(= 100 - 74 = 26\%\)

subtopic: Packing of Particles in Crystal Lattice
stem: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The atoms of element B forms ccp structure. The atoms of A occupy 1/3rd of tetrahedral voids. What is the formula of the compound?
solution:
The atoms of element B form ccp structure. The number of tetrahedral voids generated is twice the number of B atoms.

Thus, number of tetrahedral voids \(= 2\mathrm{B}\)

The atoms A occupy \((1/3)\) of these tetrahedral voids.

Hence, number of A atoms \(= 2\mathrm{B} \times 1/3\)

Ratio of A and B atoms \(= 2/3\ \mathrm{B} : 1\mathrm{B} = 2/3 : 1 = 2 : 3\)

Formula of compound \(= \mathrm{A_2B_3}\)

stem: Niobium forms bcc structure. The density of niobium is 8.55 g/cm\(^3\) and length of unit cell edge is 330.6 pm. How many atoms and unit cells are present in 0.5 g of niobium?
solution:
[Textbook misprint: in part (ii) the book's printed substitution keeps the \(\times\,2\) carried over from part (i), writing \(0.5 \times 2\) in the numerator. That contradicts the formula printed immediately above it, \(\text{number of unit cells} = x/(\rho a^3)\), which has no factor \(n\), and it also contradicts the book's own printed answer: the expression as printed evaluates to \(3.24 \times 10^{21}\), which is part (i)'s answer, whereas \(0.5/(8.55 \times (3.306 \times 10^{-8})^3) = 1.62 \times 10^{21}\), which is what the book prints. The substitution is corrected below; the printed answers of both parts are correct as they stand.]

i. Number of atoms in \(x\) g niobium \(= \dfrac{xn}{\rho a^3}\)

\(x = 0.5\ \mathrm{g}\), \(n = 2\) (for bcc structure), \(\rho = 8.55\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}\),

\(a = 330.6\ \mathrm{pm} = 3.306 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}\).

Number of atoms in 0.5 g of niobium

\(= \dfrac{0.5\ \mathrm{g} \times 2}{8.55\ \mathrm{g\ cm^{-3}} \times (3.306 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm})^3} = 3.25 \times 10^{21}\)

ii. Number of unit cells in \(x\) g \(= \dfrac{x}{\rho a^3}\)

Number of unit cells in 0.5 g of niobium

\(= \dfrac{0.5\ \mathrm{g}}{8.55\ \mathrm{g\ cm^{-3}} \times (3.306 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm})^3} = 1.62 \times 10^{21}\)

subtopic: Packing of Particles in Crystal Lattice
stem: A compound forms hcp structure. What is the number of (a) octahedral voids (b) tetrahedral voids (c) total voids formed in 0.4 mol of it.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book prints the number of atoms in 0.4 mol as \(2.4098 \times 10^{23}\); \(0.4 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 2.4088 \times 10^{23}\). The example contradicts itself, because its own part (b) prints \(4.818 \times 10^{23}\), which is \(2 \times 2.4088 \times 10^{23}\) and not \(2 \times 2.4098 \times 10^{23}\ (= 4.8196 \times 10^{23})\). The value is corrected to \(2.4088 \times 10^{23}\) below; the printed answers to (a), (b) and (c) are otherwise unaffected.]

Number of atoms in 0.4 mol \(= 0.4 \times N_A = 0.4 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 2.4088 \times 10^{23}\)

(a) Number of octahedral voids = number of atoms \(= 2.4088 \times 10^{23}\)

(b) Number of tetrahedral voids \(= 2 \times\) number of atoms \(= 2 \times 2.4088 \times 10^{23} = 4.818 \times 10^{23}\)

(c) Total number of voids \(= 2.409 \times 10^{23} + 4.818 \times 10^{23} = 7.227 \times 10^{23}\)
